014package org.microbean.scopelet;
015
016import java.util.Iterator;
017import java.util.Map.Entry;
018
019import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
020import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentMap;
021
022import java.util.concurrent.locks.Lock;
023import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;
024
025import java.util.function.Supplier;
026
027import org.microbean.bean.Factory;
028import org.microbean.bean.Request;
029
030import org.microbean.attributes.Attributes;
031
032/**
033 * A thread-safe, partial {@link Scopelet} implementation backed by {@link ConcurrentMap} machinery.
034 *
035 * @param <M> the {@link MapBackedScopelet} subclass extending this class
036 *
037 * @author <a href="https://about.me/lairdnelson" target="_top">Laird Nelson</a>
038 */
039public abstract class MapBackedScopelet<M extends MapBackedScopelet<M>> extends Scopelet<M> {
040
041  private final ConcurrentMap<Object, Instance<?>> instances;
042
043  private final ConcurrentMap<Object, ReentrantLock> creationLocks;
044
045  /**
046   * Creates a new {@link MapBackedScopelet}.
047   *
048   * @see Scopelet#Scopelet()
049   */
050  protected MapBackedScopelet() {
051    super();
052    this.creationLocks = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
053    this.instances = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
054  }
055
056  // All parameters are nullable.
057  @Override // Scopelet<M>
058  public <I> I instance(final Object beanId,
059                        final Factory<I> factory,
060                        final Request<I> request) {
061    if (!this.active()) {
062      throw new InactiveScopeletException();
063    } else if (beanId == null) {
064      return null;
065    }
066    final Supplier<? extends I> s = this.supplier(beanId, factory, request);
067    return s == null ? null : s.get();
068  }
069
070  private final <I> Supplier<I> supplier(final Object id,
071                                         final Factory<I> factory,
072                                         final Request<I> request) {
073    // (Don't use computeIfAbsent().)
074    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
075    final Supplier<I> supplier = (Supplier<I>)this.instances.get(id);
076    if (supplier != null || factory == null) {
077      // If we had a Supplier, return it, and if we didn't, and we have no means of creating a new one, return null.
078      return supplier;
079    }
080
081    // We can't use computeIfAbsent so things get a little tricky here.
082    //
083    // There wasn't anything in the instances map. So we want to effectively synchronize on instance creation. We're
084    // going to do this by maintaining Locks in a map, one per id in question. Please pay close attention to the locking
085    // semantics below.
086
087    // Create a new lock, but don't lock() it just yet.
088    final ReentrantLock newLock = new ReentrantLock();
089
090    // Atomically and gracefully lock it and put it into the creationLocks ConcurrentMap if there isn't one in there
091    // already.
092    final ReentrantLock creationLock = this.lockedCreationLock(id, newLock);
093    assert creationLock.isLocked() : "!creationLock.isLocked(): " + creationLock;
094
095    if (creationLock == newLock) {
096
097      try {
098        // (The finally block will unlock creationLock/newLock.)
099
100        // We successfully put newLock into the map so no creation was already in progress.
101        assert this.creationLocks.get(id) == newLock;
102
103        // Perform creation.
104        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
105        final Instance<I> newInstance =
106          new Instance<I>(factory == this ? (I)this : factory.create(request),
107                          factory::destroy, // Destructor
108                          request);
109
110        // Put the created instance into our instance map. There will not be a pre-existing instance.
111        final Object previous = this.instances.put(id, newInstance);
112        assert previous == null : "Unexpected prior instance: " + previous;
113
114        // Return the newly created instance.
115        return newInstance;
116
117      } finally {
118        try {
119          final Object removedLock = this.creationLocks.remove(id);
120          assert removedLock == newLock : "Unexpected removedLock: " + removedLock + "; newLock: " + newLock;
121        } finally {
122          newLock.unlock();
123        }
124      }
125    }
126
127    // There was a Lock in the creationLocks map already that was not the newLock we just created. That's either another
128    // thread performing creation (an OK situation) or we have re-entered this method on the current thread and have
129    // encountered a newLock ancestor (probably not such a great situation). In any event, "our" newLock was never
130    // inserted into the map. It will therefore be unlocked (it was never locked in the first place). Discard it in
131    // preparation for switching locks to creationLock instead.
132    assert !newLock.isLocked() : "newLock was locked: " + newLock;
133    assert !this.creationLocks.containsValue(newLock) : "Creation lock contained " + newLock + "; creationLock: " + creationLock;
134    // Lock and unlock in rapid succession. Why?  lock() will block if another thread is currently creating, and will
135    // return immediately if it is not. This is kind of a cheap way of doing Object.wait().
136    try {
137      creationLock.lock(); // potentially blocks
138    } finally {
139      creationLock.unlock();
140    }
141
142    // If we legitimately blocked in the lock() operation, then another thread was truly creating, and it is guaranteed
143    // that thread will have removed the lock from our creationLocks map. If on the other hand the lock was held by this
144    // very thread, then no blocking occurred above, and we're in a cycle, and the lock will NOT have been removed from
145    // the creationLocks map (see above). Thus we can detect cycles by blindly attempting a removal: if it returns a
146    // non-null Object, we're in a cycle, otherwise everything is cool. Moreover, it is guaranteed that if the removal
147    // returns a non-null Object, that will be the creationLock this very thread inserted earlier. No matter what, we
148    // must make sure that the creationLocks map no longer contains a lock for the id in question.
149    final Object removedLock = this.creationLocks.remove(id);
150    if (removedLock != null) {
151      assert removedLock == creationLock : "Unexpected removedLock: " + removedLock + "; creationLock: " + creationLock;
152      throw new CreationCycleDetectedException();
153    }
154    // The other thread finished creating; let's try again to pick up its results.
155    return this.supplier(id, factory, request); // RECURSIVE
156  }
157
158  @Override // Scopelet<M>
159  public boolean remove(final Object id) {
160    if (!this.active()) {
161      throw new InactiveScopeletException();
162    }
163    if (id != null) {
164      final Instance<?> instance = this.instances.remove(id);
165      if (instance != null) {
166        instance.close();
167        return true;
168      }
169    }
170    return false;
171  }
172
173  @Override // Scopelet<M>
174  public void close() {
175    if (this.closed()) {
176      return;
177    }
178    super.close(); // critical
179    final Iterator<Entry<Object, ReentrantLock>> i = this.creationLocks.entrySet().iterator();
180    while (i.hasNext()) {
181      final Entry<?, ? extends ReentrantLock> e = i.next();
182      try {
183        e.getValue().unlock();
184      } finally {
185        i.remove();
186      }
187    }
188    final Iterator<Entry<Object, Instance<?>>> i2 = this.instances.entrySet().iterator();
189    while (i2.hasNext()) {
190      final Entry<?, ? extends Instance<?>> e = i2.next();
191      try {
192        e.getValue().close();
193      } finally {
194        i2.remove();
195      }
196    }
197  }
198
199  // If candidate is not present in this.creationLocks, puts it in in a locked state atomically and returns
200  // it. Otherwise returns the pre-existing creation lock, which, by definition, will already be locked.
201  private final ReentrantLock lockedCreationLock(final Object id, final ReentrantLock candidate) {
202    if (candidate.isLocked()) {
203      throw new IllegalArgumentException("candidate.isLocked(): " + candidate);
204    }
205    try {
206      return this.creationLocks.computeIfAbsent(id, x -> lock(candidate));
207    } catch (final RuntimeException | Error justBeingCareful) {
208      // ReentrantLock#lock() is not documented to throw anything, but if it does, make sure we unlock it.
209      try {
210        candidate.unlock();
211      } catch (final RuntimeException | Error suppressMe) {
212        justBeingCareful.addSuppressed(suppressMe);
213      }
214      throw justBeingCareful;
215    }
216  }
217
218  private static final <T extends Lock> T lock(final T candidate) {
219    candidate.lock();
220    return candidate;
221  }
222
223}
